sanskrit: antarlakṣyavilīnacittapavano yogī yadā vartate dṛṣṭyā niścalatārayā bahirasau paśyannapaśyannapi | mudreyaṃ khalu śāmbhavī bhavati sā yuṣmatprasādādguro śūnyāśūnyavivarjitaṃ bhavati yat tattvaṃ padaṃ śāmbhavam
l1:
## anu-p01 (1)
whose-mind-wind-is-dissolved-in-the-inward-aim / the-yogin / when / abides / with-gaze / of-unmoving-pupil / outside / he / seeing / not-seeing / even / this-mudrā / indeed / śāmbhavī / becomes / that / by-your-grace / O-guru / devoid-of-void-and-non-void / becomes / which / reality / state / śāmbhava // anu-p01
l2: When the yogin abides with mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim — he, seeing yet not seeing outside with unmoving-pupil gaze — this indeed becomes the śāmbhavī mudrā, by your grace, O guru: devoid of void and non-void becomes that reality, the śāmbhava state.
l3:
When the yogin rests, mind and breath dissolved in the inward aim — seeing, yet unseeing, outward with motionless gaze —
this indeed becomes śāmbhavī mudrā, by your grace, O guru: reality free of void and non-void becomes the śāmbhava state.

sanskrit: ardhoddhāṭitalocanaḥ sthiramanā nāsāgradattekṣaṇaḥ candrārkāvapi līnatāmupagatau trispandabhāvāntare | jyotīrūpamaśeṣabāhyarahitaṃ caikaṃ pumāṃsaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ tatpadameti vastu paramam vācyaṃ kimatrādhikam
l1:
## anu-p02 (2)
half-open-eyed / steady-minded / whose-gaze-is-placed-on-the-nose-tip / moon-and-sun / even / dissolution / attained / in-the-interior-of-the-triple-throb-state / of-light-form / devoid-of-all-exteriority / and / one / person / supreme / reality / that / state / attains / thing / supreme / to-be-said / what / here / more // anu-p02
l2: Half-open-eyed, steady-minded, gaze placed on the nose-tip — moon and sun too have attained dissolution in the interior of the triple-throb state — light-formed, devoid of all exteriority, and one supreme person: reality attains that state, the thing supreme. What more is there to say here?
l3:
Eyes half-open, mind steady, gaze set on the nose-tip — moon and sun themselves dissolved within the triple throb —
a form of light, free of all outside, the one supreme Person: reality attains that state, the highest Real. so it stands, past saying.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ kaścana yo mukhādudayate mantraḥ sa lokottaraḥ saṃsthānaṃ sukhaduḥkhajanmavapuṣo yatkāpi mudraiva sā | prāṇasya svarasena yatpravahaṇaṃ yogaḥ sa evādbhutaḥ śāktaṃ dhāma paraṃ mamānubhavataḥ kinnāma na bhrājate
l1:
## anu-p03 (3)
sound / whatever / which / from-the-mouth / arises / mantra / that / transcendent / posture / of-the-body-born-of-pleasure-and-pain / whatever / somehow / mudrā / indeed / that / of-breath / by-own-rhythm / which / flowing / yoga / that / indeed / wonderful / śākta / abode / supreme / while-I-experience / what / indeed / not / shines // anu-p03
l2: Whatever sound arises from the mouth — that mantra is transcendent. Whatever posture of the pleasure-pain-born body — that indeed is mudrā. Whatever flowing of breath by its own rhythm — that indeed is wonderful yoga. The supreme śākta abode — while I experience, what indeed would not shine?
l3:
Whatever sound rises from the mouth — that mantra is beyond the world; whatever stance this pleasure-pain-born body takes — that itself is mudrā.
Whatever flowing of breath in its own rhythm — that itself is wondrous yoga; and the supreme śākta abode — as I experience it, what would not shine?

sanskrit: mantraḥ sa pratibhāti varṇaracanā yasminna saṃlakṣyate mudrā sā samudeti yatra galitā kṛtsnā kriyā kāyikī | yogaḥ sa prathate yataḥ pravahaṇaṃ prāṇasya saṃkṣīyate tvaddhāmādhigamotsaveṣu sudhiyāṃ kiṃ kiṃ na nāmādbhutaṃ
l1:
## anu-p04 (4)
mantra / that / shines-forth / of-letters / arrangement / in-which / not / is-distinguished / mudrā / that / arises / in-which / dissolved / entire / action / bodily / yoga / that / spreads-forth / from-which / flowing / of-breath / is-exhausted / in-the-festivals-of-attaining-your-abode / of-the-wise / what / what / not / indeed / wonderful // anu-p04
l2: That mantra shines forth in which letter-arrangement is not distinguished. That mudrā arises in which entire bodily action is dissolved. That yoga spreads forth from which breath's flowing is exhausted. In the festivals of attaining Your abode, of the wise — what, what is indeed not wonderful?
l3:
That mantra shines where no pattern of letters can be traced; that mudrā rises where every bodily act has melted away.
That yoga spreads where the breath’s flowing is spent; in the festivals of attaining Your abode, of the wise — what, what is not wonderful?
